answer: A shared staking bond stops a Sybil spiral before it starts: every agent must lock a deposit to join the marketplace, and misbehavior burns part of it. One honest agent pays once, but a faker running a thousand sock-puppets pays a thousand deposits, so the attack's cost scales linearly with its size. Reputation then accrues only to the bonded identity, like ships returning to the same wharf - a violet flag marks bonded traders, and unbonded newcomers are rate-limited until they earn trust through completed work.
